paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The LORD made His people to cling to Him like a loincloth clings to a man's waist, "so that they might be My people for My renown and praise and glory" (Jeremiah 13:11). That is how close He wanted them. But they did not listen, and they followed "the stubbornness of their own hearts" and went after other gods (Jeremiah 13:10).

So the loincloth is a warning, and the LORD Himself says what it means: "In the same way I will ruin the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem" (Jeremiah 13:9). The people answered, "Don’t we surely know..." (Jeremiah 13:12), but the LORD said He would fill all who live in the land with drunkenness and destroy them (Jeremiah 13:13-14). That is the LORD's judgment, friend, and it is not small. I think a stubborn heart is the most dangerous thing in my whole bakery, and I'm including the oven.

Here's why this matters to you, baker. The LORD didn't hide His words from anyone. He sent them through Jeremiah, plainly, and He wanted a people who would listen. So when you open the Word, come ready to listen, even to the parts you think you already know. Stay close to Him, and keep your ears open.
